title: HubSpot layoffs: CEO says job cuts are not driven by AI 'efficiencies,' but AI is still behind the sweeping changes
key_facts: HubSpot announced layoffs on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026.
About 660 workers, 7% of staff, will be laid off.
CEO Yamini Rangan said the decision 'is not driven by AI-related efficiencies'.
The company says it is shifting from building software to 'delivering outcomes' for customers with AI, with fewer management layers.
Severance is 20 weeks of base pay plus a week per year of service up to 30 weeks, and five months of healthcare.
In August HubSpot reported Q2 revenue up 20% to nearly $912 million.
quote_evidence: "Over the past year, we have shifted our strategy from building software that helps customers grow to delivering outcomes for them with AI," Rangan wrote.
She did note that the layoff decision "is not driven by AI-related efficiencies."
why_it_matters_hint: A company links layoffs to an AI-led change in strategy while denying that AI efficiency is the cause.
notes: Fast Company page blocked; same story read at CBS News Boston, which cites Rangan's letter. Fast Company's headline says AI is still behind the changes; that framing is not verified here. Status CONFIRMED because the company's own letter is quoted.
